title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: Boolean Retrieval Model
summary: The Boolean retrieval model matches documents against Boolean expressions of query terms using AND, OR, NOT operators. A document is either relevant (1) or not (0) — no ranking.

sections.title: ① Concept Explanation
sections.body: The Boolean retrieval model matches documents against Boolean expressions of query terms using AND, OR, NOT operators. A document is either relevant (1) or not (0) — no ranking. The model relies on an inverted index where each term maps to a sorted posting list of document IDs. AND queries intersect posting lists; OR queries merge them; NOT queries compute complements. While simple and deterministic, Boolean retrieval has no notion of partial matching or term weighting, making it unsuitable for ranked retrieval without extensions (e.g., weighted Boolean).

sections.title: ④ Visual Explanation
sections.body:
```
BOOLEAN RETRIEVAL — INVERTED INDEX AND OPERATIONS
══════════════════════════════════════════════════

Inverted Index:
  "python"  → [1, 3, 5, 7, 12]
  "tutorial"→ [2, 3, 8, 12]
  "guide"   → [1, 4, 7, 9]

Query: "python AND tutorial"
  List1: [1, 3, 5,  7, 12]
          ↑
  List2: [2, 3, 8, 12]
          ↑
  Step 1: 1 < 2 → advance i      [1]→skip
  Step 2: 3 = 3 → MATCH! [3]     [3]→emit
  Step 3: 5 > 3 → advance j      [3]→skip
  Step 4: 5 < 8 → advance i      [5]→skip
  Step 5: 7 < 8 → advance i      [7]→skip
  Step 6: 12 > 8 → advance j     [8]→skip
  Step 7: 12 = 12 → MATCH! [12]
  Result: [3, 12]

Query: "python OR guide"
  List1: [1, 3, 5, 7, 12]
  List2: [1, 4, 7, 9]
  Result: [1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12]  ← union

Query: "python AND NOT guide"
  python: [1, 3, 5, 7, 12]
  guide:  [1, 4, 7, 9]
  Result: [3, 5, 12]              ← setdiff
```

quiz.question: How does an AND query work on an inverted index?
options: When the presence/absence of key terms is the primary relevance signal.
An inverted index maps each unique term to a list (posting list) of document IDs where that term appears, with optional frequency and position data.
Given a static document collection and a new query, retrieve the most relevant documents.
Retrieve posting lists for each term, then intersect them. Use the shortest posting list first to minimise work.
quiz.explanation: Retrieve posting lists for each term, then intersect them. Use the shortest posting list first to minimise work. Merge in O(P₁ + P₂) using two-pointer technique.

quiz.question: How does an OR query work?
options: No. Cosine similarity is length-invariant.
(1) Vocabulary mismatch (no synonym handling). (2) All common terms get low IDF — the model degrades on queries with only high-frequency terms.
Databases retrieve exact matches on structured data with SQL.
Merge (union) two sorted posting lists in O(P₁ + P₂). Returns all documents containing either term — maximises recall.
quiz.explanation: Merge (union) two sorted posting lists in O(P₁ + P₂). Returns all documents containing either term — maximises recall.

quiz.question: What is the NOT operator's limitation in IR?
options: A retrieval model defines how to measure relevance between query and document.
An information need is the underlying intent ("I want to understand BM25 tuning").
As a vector where each dimension is the TF-IDF weight of the query term.
NOT alone returns the complement of a posting list — potentially millions of documents.
quiz.explanation: NOT alone returns the complement of a posting list — potentially millions of documents. It must be combined with AND (e.g., "python AND NOT snake") to be useful. Standalone NOT is computationally dangerous.

quiz.question: How do you process a query with multiple Boolean operators efficiently?
options: (1) Boolean model, (2) Vector Space Model (TF-IDF), (3) Probabilistic model (BM25, BIM), (4) Language Model (query likelihood), (5) Neural/Dense retrieval (bi-encoders).
Dot product favours longer documents because they have larger magnitude vectors.
(1) All-or-nothing — no partial matching. (2) Query formulation burden on user.
Parse into a query tree. Evaluate bottom-up.
quiz.explanation: Parse into a query tree. Evaluate bottom-up. For AND nodes, sort operands by ascending posting list length to minimise intermediate result sizes.

quiz.question: What is a proximity operator in extended Boolean retrieval?
options: Assumes: (1) terms are binary (present/absent), (2) terms are independent, (3) relevance is binary.
A document "borrows" μ pseudo-counts from the collection distribution.
Maximum likelihood over the entire corpus: P(t|C) = total_count(t) / total_tokens.
/n or NEAR(n) — requires two terms to appear within n positions of each other.
quiz.explanation: /n or NEAR(n) — requires two terms to appear within n positions of each other. Needs a positional inverted index that stores term positions, not just doc IDs.
